studies.title: Meta's Economic Contribution in the U.S. (2024)
studies.claim: Applying the BEA multipliers to Meta-supported advertiser revenue estimates and Meta's own non-advertising revenues, we find that $548 billion in economic activity and 3.4 million total jobs is linked to US supply chains relying on our platforms in 2024.

source.label: Meta Research, Economic Contribution study page (U.S. only, 2024)
source.quote: we find that $548 billion in economic activity and 3.4 million total jobs is linked to US supply chains relying on our platforms in 2024.

ecosystem.notes: The FY2025 10-K has no flow measure, so measure is null. The study is still Meta's own 2024 U.S. estimate: the study page, rechecked November 24, 2026, still reports 2024 figures, and no newer edition was found, so it is kept. It was announced May 13, 2025 ("a new study we conducted") and covers the U.S. only. It starts from Meta's estimate that each U.S. ad dollar yields $3.71 of advertiser revenue ("over $215 billion in business/advertisers revenues in the U.S. from Meta ads"), then applies BEA input-output multipliers for indirect and induced activity, so the $548 billion is a modelled economic-activity figure, not money paid to businesses or creators. It includes about $2 billion of Meta's own non-advertising sales. The study year (2024) is a year earlier than the platform revenue (FY2025), and Meta revenue is worldwide, so the two are not comparable.
